newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sets up unified arms export firm.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sets up unified arms export firm.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has combined the operations of its three arms export firms in a bid to boost sales and tighten controls over the industry, a government official said on Tuesday.

Volodymyr Karkanytsya, deputy head of the government's military complex and conversion department, said a single, new company, Ukrspetsexport, would take over the obligations and assets of the firms Progress, Ukrinmash and Ukroboronservice.
"This is a normal, civilised decision which will increase the control of the state over all weaponry sales abroad," Karkanytsya said.
"Ukraine is far behind the world's top arms exporters and we have no illusions. But we believe this step will boost sales on the world market," he added.
Last August Ukraine won a tender in Pakistan to supply Islamabad with 320 T-80UD tanks for $580 million over four years -- hailed by Kiev as a "breakthrough" to the world arms market.
After the collapse of the former Soviet Union in 1991 Ukraine inherited one-third of its military facilities.
But the industry was bogged down for several years due to a lack of funds and purchases as well as severed economic links with the military industries of other former Soviet republics.
Ukraine earned $74 million from arms sales last year according to Western estimates, but government sources put the figure at more than $100 million.
Ukrainian officials say the defence industry's potential could provide at least several billion dollars a year.

Last year Ukraine supplied 300 10-tonne trucks to Indian armed forces, traditionally a buyer of Soviet equipment, and last July clinched a deal with New Delhi to supply a new 6.5-tonne military truck.

Another deal was announced recently to provide Sri Lanka's air force with four Antonov An-32 military transport planes. Kiev also signed a deal with Egypt to repair 10 MiG-21 fighters. Two years ago Ukraine shipped 56 air-to-air missiles to China.
Earlier this year U.S. media said An-32B cargo planes sold or leased by Ukrainian were in use on traditional cocaine smuggling routes in Colombia, Peru, Panama and Mexico.
But the Ukrainian leadership denied this. "We don't violate international norms of arms sales," Karkanytsya said. "There is no single proved case of any violation."
